reasons: Tests were not run while writing these notes.
Coverage looks thorough for conflicts, units and options.

terms.meaning: one statement of a value taken from a document, such as a 20 ft depth
the step that compares all claims and decides which ones can be used
two claims about the same item that disagree
two independent sources that agree on the same value
a generic design rule value that must be assigned to a real item before use
one choice among several alternatives in a design
a value converted into the model's standard unit
whether a claim applies to this project, another project, or in general
a refusal raised when data does not meet the rules

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for claim tests
sections.what: Brings in the claim data types and reconciliation functions that every test here uses.
sections.why: Likely reason: each test builds claims and runs the same reconciliation step.
sections.watch_out: Renaming a type in the contracts module breaks every test in this file.

sections.name: claim
sections.title: Builds a sample measured claim
sections.what: Creates one claim for the depth of a dead-end foundation from a conceptual drawing, with configurable identifier, value, unit and extra context.
sections.why: Likely reason: each test starts from one valid claim and changes only what it needs.
sections.watch_out: Default values are shared by all tests, so changing a default can change many results.

sections.name: test_conflict_blocks_only_affected_property_and_preserves_inputs
sections.title: Conflicting values block only the affected property
sections.what: Two claims disagree on the same foundation depth and a third, unrelated claim is about a house width. Confirms both depth claims are marked conflicting and need review, the width still passes, the original inputs are unchanged, and the depth stored in metres is correct.
sections.why: Likely reason: one dispute should not stop the whole model.
sections.watch_out: Changing how subjects are matched could make unrelated items conflict or let real conflicts slip past.

sections.name: test_exact_units_corroborate_only_independent_contents
sections.title: Same value from different sources strengthens a claim
sections.what: Two claims with equal values from the same source file produce no conflict. Two claims from different source files are marked corroborated, yet still count as one model assertion.
sections.why: Likely reason: so a fact repeated in two documents is not counted twice.
sections.watch_out: Source file hashes decide independence, so a shared hash makes two sources look like one.

sections.name: test_context_cannot_become_installed_asset_or_override_project
sections.title: Context cannot override the project or become an asset
sections.what: Gives reference claims from another project, general context, a standard, a vendor go-by, a manual, unspecified authority, a future reservation, or a material or labour role. Confirms only the project claim is used and no conflict arises.
sections.why: Likely reason: reference material should inform reviewers without changing the model.
sections.watch_out: Each new applicability or role label must be added here so it cannot silently change the model.

sections.name: test_standard_requires_explicit_project_asset_assignment
sections.title: Standards need explicit assignment
sections.what: A standard rule is used only when it is explicitly assigned to a project asset. A claim with no source basis raises a validation error naming project identity and source basis.
sections.why: Likely reason: generic standard values must not be applied to a real item without a decision.

sections.name: test_missing_unit_and_calendar_days_are_not_silently_normalized
sections.title: Missing units and day or hour values not guessed
sections.what: A claim with no unit is not used. Calendar days and hours for the same item are not converted into each other, so the pair is marked conflicted.
sections.why: Likely reason: a day can mean different durations, so the code will not guess.
sections.watch_out: Adding automatic day conversion would change these results.

sections.name: test_same_claim_id_is_idempotent_but_inconsistent_payload_fails
sections.title: Repeated claim fine, changed payload fails
sections.what: Feeding the same claim twice counts it once. Feeding the same identifier with a different value raises an error. A renamed copy keeps the same identifier.
sections.why: Likely reason: the identifier fingerprints the claim's meaning, so repeats are harmless but changes must be noticed.
sections.watch_out: What goes into the identifier decides what counts as a repeat, so change it carefully.

sections.name: test_revision_and_filename_date_do_not_approve_larger_value
sections.title: Revision date and file name do not approve a value
sections.what: A later revision with a newer date, and a file named as approved, do not make a larger value usable. Neither claim is used.
sections.why: Likely reason: those hints are not proof of approval.

sections.name: test_equal_subset_not_in_conflicting_reference_list
sections.title: Matching claims kept out of the conflict list
sections.what: Of three claims, two agree and one differs. The differing claim lists both agreeing claims as conflicts, while the agreeing claims list only the differing one.
sections.why: Likely reason: so identical duplicates do not show up as disputes with each other.

sections.name: test_legacy_serialization_stays_unchanged_without_claim_metadata
sections.title: Old records save the same way
sections.what: A record with no claim details is saved without the new claim fields and is still usable.
sections.why: Likely reason: so older saved data still loads and works.

sections.name: test_nonfinite_claim_rejected
sections.title: Not-a-number values rejected
sections.what: A claim whose value is NaN is refused with a finite-value error.
sections.why: Likely reason: NaN breaks comparisons and calculations.

sections.name: test_dimensionally_wrong_or_unknown_unit_cannot_drive_length
sections.title: Wrong or unknown units cannot drive a length
sections.what: Units such as furlong, each, a single letter, a blank, or unknown are refused as length sources, either because they are not lengths or the model does not know them.
sections.why: Likely reason: a length from an unknown unit would be wrong by an unknown amount.
sections.watch_out: A new unit added to the known list needs its correct dimension and conversion.

sections.name: test_raw_and_shared_values_must_be_identical
sections.title: Stored and shared values must match exactly
sections.what: Changing the stored value or unit on a record with claim details causes a validation error about shared evidence.
sections.why: Likely reason: the two copies of the value must never disagree.

sections.name: test_aliases_reconcile_once_and_reimports_are_permutation_invariant
sections.title: Aliases merge once, results same in any order
sections.what: The same claim imported under another identifier and file name is folded into one. The result is identical whatever order the claims arrive in, and reprocessing the output gives the same result.
sections.why: Likely reason: so repeated imports are reproducible.
sections.watch_out: Output order must never change saved results, so any sorting change needs this test.

sections.name: test_case_and_whitespace_cannot_evade_property_conflict
sections.title: Spacing and capitals cannot hide a conflict
sections.what: A second claim with different spacing and capital letters in its project, subject and fact type is treated as the same item, so the disagreement is caught.
sections.why: Likely reason: text from documents is inconsistent, and small differences must not hide a real clash.

sections.name: test_option_requires_selected_assignment_source_not_extraction_acceptance
sections.title: Options need a selected source
sections.what: An unselected option is not used. Marking an option as selected without a selection basis is refused. With a basis it is used, and a superseded option is not used.
sections.why: Likely reason: one option out of several must be chosen by a document, not by extraction alone.

sections.name: test_quantitative_property_requires_a_finite_numeric_scalar
sections.title: Quantities must be one finite number
sections.what: A claim whose value is true, a list, or a text string is not usable as a quantity.
sections.why: Likely reason: only real numbers can drive a size.

sections.name: test_oversized_integer_eligibility_fails_closed
sections.title: Huge whole numbers fail safely
sections.what: Very large positive or negative whole numbers are not used, without crashing the check.
sections.why: Likely reason: extremely large numbers can break unit conversion.

sections.name: test_raw_equality_distinguishes_booleans_from_numbers
sections.title: True is not the same as one
sections.what: The stored value and raw value must match in type as well as number, so true is not treated as one and false not as zero.
sections.why: Likely reason: in Python true equals one, so the type must be checked too.
sections.watch_out: Equality checks in this area must consider type as well as value.

sections.name: test_invalid_option_states_fail_closed
sections.title: Bad option states fail loudly
sections.what: A superseded option without a name, a blank option name, or a blank name with a selected status each raise an error about options.
sections.why: Likely reason: an unclear option choice must be refused rather than guessed.

sections.name: test_removing_or_rejecting_conflict_does_not_leave_dangling_edges_or_approve
sections.title: Removing a conflict leaves no stale links
sections.what: When a conflicting claim is removed or rejected, the surviving claim has no leftover conflict links and is not approved. A rejected claim also clears the links.
sections.why: Likely reason: stale links would wrongly block or mislabel claims later.

summary: Tests the rules that decide which measured facts from project documents can be used in the 3D model and which conflict with each other.
purpose: Makes sure disagreements between documents are shown for review rather than silently resolved, and that reference or unapproved values never change the model.
why: Likely reason: schedules, drawings and specifications often contradict one another, so the app must surface conflicts. Reason not stated in the code beyond this.
how: Each test builds claims with a shared helper, runs the reconciliation step, and checks which claims are usable, which conflict, and the review status. Some tests also save the result and compare it again.
inputs: Claim records built in test code with values, units, source details and context labels.
outputs: Pass or fail results from pytest.
risks: Tests depend on the lists of allowed units and context labels. Changing those lists may require updating these tests.
debug: Find the failing test name, then check the claims it builds and the conflict and review status the assertion compares.
